passages.text: When it was decided that we would sail for Italy, Paul and some other prisoners were handed over to a centurion named Julius, who belonged to the Imperial Regiment.
passages.sermon:
Paul was a prisoner.
Some other men were also prisoners.
The authorities decided we would sail to Italy.
They handed Paul and the other prisoners over to a centurion.
The centurion’s name was Julius.
Julius belonged to the Imperial Regiment.
passages.original: Ὡς δὲ ἐκρίθη τοῦ ἀποπλεῖν ἡμᾶς εἰς τὴν Ἰταλίαν παρεδίδουν τόν τε Παῦλον καί τινας ἑτέρους δεσμώτας ἑκατοντάρχῃ ὀνόματι Ἰουλίῳ σπείρης Σεβαστῆς

passages.text: We boarded an Adramyttian ship about to sail for ports along the coast of Asia, and we put out to sea. Aristarchus, a Macedonian from Thessalonica, was with us.
passages.sermon:
Paul was a prisoner.
Julius was a centurion of the Imperial Regiment.
Some other prisoners were with Paul.
We boarded a ship from Adramyttium.
This ship was about to sail to ports along the coast of Asia.
We set out to sea.
Aristarchus was with us.
Aristarchus was a Macedonian.
Aristarchus was from Thessalonica.
passages.original: ἐπιβάντες δὲ πλοίῳ Ἀδραμυττηνῷ μέλλοντι πλεῖν εἰς τοὺς κατὰ τὴν Ἀσίαν τόπους ἀνήχθημεν ὄντος σὺν ἡμῖν Ἀριστάρχου Μακεδόνος Θεσσαλονικέως

passages.text: The next day we landed at Sidon, and Julius treated Paul with consideration, allowing him to visit his friends and receive their care.
passages.sermon:
Paul was a prisoner.
Julius was a centurion.
Julius belonged to the Imperial Regiment.
The next day, we landed at Sidon.
Julius treated Paul kindly.
Julius allowed Paul to visit his friends.
Paul received care from his friends.
passages.original: Τῇ τε ἑτέρᾳ κατήχθημεν εἰς Σιδῶνα φιλανθρώπως τε ὁ Ἰούλιος τῷ Παύλῳ χρησάμενος ἐπέτρεψεν πρὸς τοὺς φίλους πορευθέντι ἐπιμελείας τυχεῖν

passages.text: After putting out from there, we sailed to the lee of Cyprus because the winds were against us.
passages.sermon:
We left Sidon.
We sailed again.
The winds were against us.
We sailed to the sheltered side of Cyprus.
passages.original: κἀκεῖθεν ἀναχθέντες ὑπεπλεύσαμεν τὴν Κύπρον διὰ τὸ τοὺς ἀνέμους εἶναι ἐναντίους

passages.text: And when we had sailed across the open sea off the coast of Cilicia and Pamphylia, we came to Myra in Lycia.
passages.sermon:
Paul was a prisoner on a journey to Rome.
A centurion named Julius guarded Paul and other prisoners.
We sailed across the open sea.
The sea was near the regions of Cilicia and Pamphylia.
We traveled past these coasts.
We arrived at a city called Myra.
Myra was in the region of Lycia.
passages.original: τό τε πέλαγος τὸ κατὰ τὴν Κιλικίαν καὶ Παμφυλίαν διαπλεύσαντες κατήλθομεν εἰς Μύρα τῆς Λυκίας

passages.text: There the centurion found an Alexandrian ship sailing for Italy and put us on board.
passages.sermon:
A centurion was with us.
He found a ship from Alexandria.
This ship was sailing to Italy.
The centurion put us on this ship.
passages.original: Κἀκεῖ εὑρὼν ὁ ἑκατοντάρχης πλοῖον Ἀλεξανδρῖνον πλέον εἰς τὴν Ἰταλίαν ἐνεβίβασεν ἡμᾶς εἰς αὐτό

passages.text: After sailing slowly for many days, we arrived off Cnidus. When the wind impeded us, we sailed to the lee of Crete, opposite Salmone.
passages.sermon:
Paul was traveling by ship as a prisoner under Roman guard.
The ship sailed slowly for many days.
The travelers struggled to make progress.
They finally reached the area near Cnidus.
The wind did not allow them to continue on their planned course.
They changed direction.
They sailed to the sheltered side of Crete.
They passed opposite a place called Salmone.
passages.original: Ἐν ἱκαναῖς δὲ ἡμέραις βραδυπλοοῦντες καὶ μόλις γενόμενοι κατὰ τὴν Κνίδον μὴ προσεῶντος ἡμᾶς τοῦ ἀνέμου ὑπεπλεύσαμεν τὴν Κρήτην κατὰ Σαλμώνην

passages.text: After we had moved along the coast with difficulty, we came to a place called Fair Havens, near the town of Lasea.
passages.sermon:
Paul and his companions traveled by ship.
They moved along the coast with difficulty.
They came to a place called Fair Havens.
Fair Havens was near the town of Lasea.
passages.original: μόλις τε παραλεγόμενοι αὐτὴν ἤλθομεν εἰς τόπον τινὰ καλούμενον Καλοὺς Λιμένας ᾧ ἐγγὺς ἦν πόλις Λασαία

passages.text: By now much time had passed, and the voyage had already become dangerous because it was after the Fast. So Paul advised them, “Men, I can see that our voyage will be filled with disaster and great loss, not only to ship and cargo, but to our own lives as well.”
passages.sermon:
Paul was a Christian apostle and prisoner on a ship.
Much time had passed during the voyage.
The journey had become dangerous.
It was now after the Fast.
Paul spoke to the men on the ship.
He gave them advice.
Paul said, “Men, I see that this voyage will bring disaster.
There will be great loss.
We will lose not only the cargo and the ship.
We will also risk our own lives.”
passages.original: Ἱκανοῦ δὲ χρόνου διαγενομένου καὶ ὄντος ἤδη ἐπισφαλοῦς τοῦ πλοὸς διὰ τὸ καὶ τὴν Νηστείαν ἤδη παρεληλυθέναι παρῄνει ὁ Παῦλος λέγων αὐτοῖς Ἄνδρες θεωρῶ ὅτι μετὰ ὕβρεως καὶ πολλῆς ζημίας οὐ μόνον τοῦ φορτίου καὶ τοῦ πλοίου ἀλλὰ καὶ τῶν ψυχῶν ἡμῶν μέλλειν ἔσεσθαι τὸν πλοῦν

passages.text: But contrary to Paul’s advice, the centurion was persuaded by the pilot and by the owner of the ship.
passages.sermon:
A centurion was in charge.
A centurion listened to advice about the voyage.
Paul gave advice to the centurion.
Paul warned about danger and loss.
A pilot and a ship owner also gave advice.
The centurion trusted the pilot and the ship owner more than Paul.
The centurion chose to follow the pilot and the ship owner.
The centurion did not follow Paul’s warning.
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ ἑκατοντάρχης τῷ κυβερνήτῃ καὶ τῷ ναυκλήρῳ μᾶλλον ἐπείθετο ἢ τοῖς ὑπὸ Παύλου λεγομένοις

passages.text: Since the harbor was unsuitable to winter in, the majority decided to sail on, if somehow they could reach Phoenix to winter there. Phoenix was a harbor in Crete facing both southwest and northwest.
passages.sermon:
The harbor was not good for spending the winter.
Most of the people decided to leave the harbor.
They wanted to sail on from there.
They hoped they could reach Phoenix.
Phoenix was a harbor in Crete.
Phoenix faced southwest and northwest.
They wanted to spend the winter in Phoenix.
passages.original: ἀνευθέτου δὲ τοῦ λιμένος ὑπάρχοντος πρὸς παραχειμασίαν οἱ πλείονες ἔθεντο βουλὴν ἀναχθῆναι ἐκεῖθεν εἴ πως δύναιντο καταντήσαντες εἰς Φοίνικα παραχειμάσαι λιμένα τῆς Κρήτης βλέποντα κατὰ λίβα καὶ κατὰ χῶρον

passages.text: When a gentle south wind began to blow, they thought they had their opportunity. So they weighed anchor and sailed along, hugging the coast of Crete.
passages.sermon:
A gentle south wind began to blow.
The people on the ship saw this wind.
They believed this was their chance to leave.
They raised the anchor.
They sailed along the coast of Crete.
They stayed close to the land as they traveled.
passages.original: Ὑποπνεύσαντος δὲ νότου δόξαντες τῆς προθέσεως κεκρατηκέναι ἄραντες ἆσσον παρελέγοντο τὴν Κρήτην

passages.text: But it was not long before a cyclone called the Northeaster swept down across the island.
passages.sermon:
A cyclone came quickly.
People called this cyclone the Northeaster.
The cyclone swept down across the island.
It did not take long for this to happen.
passages.original: μετ’ οὐ πολὺ δὲ ἔβαλεν κατ’ αὐτῆς ἄνεμος τυφωνικὸς ὁ καλούμενος Εὐρακύλων

passages.text: Unable to head into the wind, the ship was caught up. So we gave way and let ourselves be driven along.
passages.sermon:
A violent wind called the Northeaster struck the ship.
The ship could not face the wind.
The wind caught the ship.
We could not control the ship.
We stopped resisting the wind.
We let the wind drive us along.
passages.original: συναρπασθέντος δὲ τοῦ πλοίου καὶ μὴ δυναμένου ἀντοφθαλμεῖν τῷ ἀνέμῳ ἐπιδόντες ἐφερόμεθα

passages.text: Passing to the lee of a small island called Cauda, we barely managed to secure the lifeboat.
passages.sermon:
Paul and his companions sailed near a small island.
The island was called Cauda.
They passed to the sheltered side of the island.
They struggled to control the ship.
They barely managed to secure the lifeboat.
passages.original: Νησίον δέ τι ὑποδραμόντες καλούμενον Καῦδα ἰσχύσαμεν μόλις περικρατεῖς γενέσθαι τῆς σκάφης

passages.text: After hoisting it up, the crew used ropes to undergird the ship. And fearing that they would run aground on the sandbars of Syrtis, they lowered the sea anchor and were driven along.
passages.sermon:
The crew hoisted up the lifeboat.
They used ropes to secure the ship underneath.
They feared they would run aground on the sandbars of Syrtis.
They lowered the sea anchor.
The wind drove the ship along.
passages.original: ἣν ἄραντες βοηθείαις ἐχρῶντο ὑποζωννύντες τὸ πλοῖον φοβούμενοί τε μὴ εἰς τὴν Σύρτιν ἐκπέσωσιν χαλάσαντες τὸ σκεῦος οὕτως ἐφέροντο

passages.text: We were tossed so violently that the next day the men began to jettison the cargo.
passages.sermon:
A violent storm tossed us.
This happened to everyone on the ship.
The next day, the men began to throw the cargo overboard.
They did this to lighten the ship.
passages.original: Σφοδρῶς δὲ χειμαζομένων ἡμῶν τῇ ἑξῆς ἐκβολὴν ἐποιοῦντο

passages.text: On the third day, they threw the ship’s tackle overboard with their own hands.
passages.sermon:
The crew faced a violent storm at sea.
On the third day, the crew acted themselves.
They took the ship’s tackle.
They threw the tackle overboard with their own hands.
passages.original: καὶ τῇ τρίτῃ αὐτόχειρες τὴν σκευὴν τοῦ πλοίου ἔρριψαν

passages.text: When neither sun nor stars appeared for many days and the great storm continued to batter us, we abandoned all hope of being saved.
passages.sermon:
Paul was a prisoner on a ship with other men.
A violent storm struck the ship.
The storm lasted for many days.
We could not see the sun.
We could not see the stars.
The storm did not stop.
The storm was very strong.
We lost all hope of being saved.
passages.original: μήτε δὲ ἡλίου μήτε ἄστρων ἐπιφαινόντων ἐπὶ πλείονας ἡμέρας χειμῶνός τε οὐκ ὀλίγου ἐπικειμένου λοιπὸν περιῃρεῖτο ἐλπὶς πᾶσα τοῦ σῴζεσθαι ἡμᾶς

passages.text: After the men had gone a long time without food, Paul stood up among them and said, “Men, you should have followed my advice not to sail from Crete. Then you would have averted this disaster and loss.
passages.sermon:
Paul was a servant of God.
Paul was among the men on the ship.
The men had not eaten for a long time.
Paul stood up in the middle of them.
Paul spoke to the men.
Paul said, “Men, you should have listened to me.
You should not have sailed from Crete.
If you had obeyed me, you would have avoided this disaster.
You would not have suffered this loss.”
passages.original: Πολλῆς τε ἀσιτίας ὑπαρχούσης τότε σταθεὶς ὁ Παῦλος ἐν μέσῳ αὐτῶν εἶπεν Ἔδει μέν ὦ ἄνδρες πειθαρχήσαντάς μοι μὴ ἀνάγεσθαι ἀπὸ τῆς Κρήτης κερδῆσαί τε τὴν ὕβριν ταύτην καὶ τὴν ζημίαν

passages.text: But now I urge you to keep up your courage, because you will not experience any loss of life, but only of the ship.
passages.sermon:
Paul spoke to the men on the ship.
He urged them to keep up their courage.
He said no one among them would lose their life.
He said only the ship would be lost.
passages.original: καὶ τὰ νῦν παραινῶ ὑμᾶς εὐθυμεῖν ἀποβολὴ γὰρ ψυχῆς οὐδεμία ἔσται ἐξ ὑμῶν πλὴν τοῦ πλοίου

passages.text: For just last night an angel of God, whose I am and whom I serve, stood beside me and said, ‘Do not be afraid, Paul; you must stand before Caesar. And look, God has granted you the lives of all who sail with you.’
passages.sermon:
Paul was a servant of God.
Paul belonged to God.
Paul served God.
Last night, an angel from God stood beside Paul.
The angel spoke to Paul.
The angel said, “Do not be afraid, Paul.”
The angel said, “You must stand before Caesar.”
The angel said, “God has given you the lives of all who sail with you.”
passages.original: παρέστη γάρ μοι ταύτῃ τῇ νυκτὶ τοῦ Θεοῦ οὗ εἰμι ἐγώ ᾧ καὶ λατρεύω ἄγγελος λέγων Μὴ φοβοῦ Παῦλε Καίσαρί σε δεῖ παραστῆναι καὶ ἰδοὺ κεχάρισταί σοι ὁ Θεὸς πάντας τοὺς πλέοντας μετὰ σοῦ

passages.text: So take courage, men, for I believe God that it will happen just as He told me.
passages.sermon:
Paul spoke to the men on the ship.
Paul was a servant of God.
Paul told them to take courage.
Paul said, "I believe God."
God told Paul what would happen.
Paul believed it would happen exactly as God said.
passages.original: Διὸ εὐθυμεῖτε ἄνδρες πιστεύω γὰρ τῷ Θεῷ ὅτι οὕτως ἔσται καθ’ ὃν τρόπον λελάληταί μοι

passages.text: However, we must run aground on some island.”
passages.sermon:
We must run aground.
We will run aground on an island.
We do not know which island.
This will happen to us.
passages.original: εἰς νῆσον δέ τινα δεῖ ἡμᾶς ἐκπεσεῖν

passages.text: On the fourteenth night we were still being driven across the Adriatic Sea. About midnight the sailors sensed they were approaching land.
passages.sermon:
Paul was on a ship with other men.
They were traveling across the Adriatic Sea.
The wind and waves drove the ship for many days.
It was now the fourteenth night.
It was midnight.
The sailors sensed they were getting close to land.
passages.original: Ὡς δὲ τεσσαρεσκαιδεκάτη νὺξ ἐγένετο διαφερομένων ἡμῶν ἐν τῷ Ἀδρίᾳ κατὰ μέσον τῆς νυκτὸς ὑπενόουν οἱ ναῦται προσάγειν τινὰ αὐτοῖς χώραν

passages.text: They took soundings and found that the water was twenty fathoms deep. Going a little farther, they took another set of soundings that read fifteen fathoms.
passages.sermon:
The sailors took soundings.
They measured the depth of the water.
They found the water was twenty fathoms deep.
They moved a short distance farther.
They took soundings again.
They found the water was fifteen fathoms deep.
passages.original: καὶ βολίσαντες εὗρον ὀργυιὰς εἴκοσι βραχὺ δὲ διαστήσαντες καὶ πάλιν βολίσαντες εὗρον ὀργυιὰς δεκαπέντε

passages.text: Fearing that we would run aground on the rocks, they dropped four anchors from the stern and prayed for daybreak.
passages.sermon:
The sailors feared danger.
They thought the ship might run aground on the rocks.
They acted to protect everyone on board.
They dropped four anchors from the stern of the ship.
They prayed for daylight to come.
passages.original: φοβούμενοί τε μή που κατὰ τραχεῖς τόπους ἐκπέσωμεν ἐκ πρύμνης ῥίψαντες ἀγκύρας τέσσαρας ηὔχοντο ἡμέραν γενέσθαι

passages.text: Meanwhile, the sailors attempted to escape from the ship. Pretending to lower anchors from the bow, they let the lifeboat down into the sea.
passages.sermon:
The sailors were on the ship.
The sailors tried to escape from the ship.
They pretended to lower anchors from the front of the ship.
They let the lifeboat down into the sea.
passages.original: Τῶν δὲ ναυτῶν ζητούντων φυγεῖν ἐκ τοῦ πλοίου καὶ χαλασάντων τὴν σκάφην εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν προφάσει ὡς ἐκ πρῴρης ἀγκύρας μελλόντων ἐκτείνειν

passages.text: But Paul said to the centurion and the soldiers, “Unless these men remain with the ship, you cannot be saved.”
passages.sermon:
Paul was a prisoner on a ship during a dangerous storm.
Paul spoke to the centurion and the soldiers.
Paul said, “These men must stay on the ship.
If these men do not stay on the ship, you cannot be saved.”
passages.original: εἶπεν ὁ Παῦλος τῷ ἑκατοντάρχῃ καὶ τοῖς στρατιώταις Ἐὰν μὴ οὗτοι μείνωσιν ἐν τῷ πλοίῳ ὑμεῖς σωθῆναι οὐ δύνασθε

passages.text: So the soldiers cut the ropes to the lifeboat and set it adrift.
passages.sermon: The soldiers acted quickly.\r\nThey cut the ropes of the lifeboat.\r\nThey let the lifeboat drift away.
passages.original: τότε ἀπέκοψαν οἱ στρατιῶται τὰ σχοινία τῆς σκάφης καὶ εἴασαν αὐτὴν ἐκπεσεῖν

passages.text: Right up to daybreak, Paul kept urging them all to eat: “Today is your fourteenth day in constant suspense, without taking any food.
passages.sermon:
Paul was a prisoner on a ship during a dangerous voyage.
Paul spoke to everyone on the ship.
Paul urged them to eat food.
Paul kept urging them until daybreak.
Paul said, “Today is your fourteenth day.”
Paul said, “You have waited in suspense for fourteen days.”
Paul said, “You have not eaten anything during this time.”
passages.original: Ἄχρι δὲ οὗ ἡμέρα ἤμελλεν γίνεσθαι παρεκάλει ὁ Παῦλος ἅπαντας μεταλαβεῖν τροφῆς λέγων Τεσσαρεσκαιδεκάτην σήμερον ἡμέραν προσδοκῶντες ἄσιτοι διατελεῖτε μηθὲν προσλαβόμενοι

passages.text: So for your own preservation, I urge you to eat something, because not a single hair of your head will be lost.”
passages.sermon:
Paul spoke to the people on the ship.
Paul urged them to eat food.
He said, "This food will help you stay safe."
He promised, "Not one of you will lose even a single hair from your head."
Paul wanted everyone to know they would be safe.
passages.original: διὸ παρακαλῶ ὑμᾶς μεταλαβεῖν τροφῆς τοῦτο γὰρ πρὸς τῆς ὑμετέρας σωτηρίας ὑπάρχει οὐδενὸς γὰρ ὑμῶν θρὶξ ἀπὸ τῆς κεφαλῆς ἀπολεῖται

passages.text: After he had said this, Paul took bread and gave thanks to God in front of them all. Then he broke it and began to eat.
passages.sermon:
Paul spoke to everyone on the ship.
He took bread.
He gave thanks to God.
He did this in front of all the people.
He broke the bread.
He began to eat.
passages.original: Εἴπας δὲ ταῦτα καὶ λαβὼν ἄρτον εὐχαρίστησεν τῷ Θεῷ ἐνώπιον πάντων καὶ κλάσας ἤρξατο ἐσθίειν

passages.text: They were all encouraged and took some food themselves.
passages.sermon:
Paul was on a ship with 275 other people.
Paul spoke to everyone and encouraged them.
All the people felt encouraged.
Each person took some food and ate.
passages.original: εὔθυμοι δὲ γενόμενοι πάντες καὶ αὐτοὶ προσελάβοντο τροφῆς

passages.text: In all, there were 276 of us on board.
passages.sermon: There were 276 people on the ship.\r\nAll of us were on board together.
passages.original: ἤμεθα δὲ αἱ πᾶσαι ψυχαὶ ἐν τῷ πλοίῳ διακόσιαι ἑβδομήκοντα ἕξ

passages.text: After the men had eaten their fill, they lightened the ship by throwing the grain into the sea.
passages.sermon:
The men ate until they were full.
They finished their meal.
They wanted to make the ship lighter.
They threw the grain into the sea.
This helped to lighten the ship.
passages.original: κορεσθέντες δὲ τροφῆς ἐκούφιζον τὸ πλοῖον ἐκβαλλόμενοι τὸν σῖτον εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν

passages.text: When daylight came, they did not recognize the land, but they sighted a bay with a sandy beach, where they decided to run the ship aground if they could.
passages.sermon:
Daylight came.
The people on the ship looked at the land.
They did not recognize the land.
They saw a bay.
The bay had a sandy beach.
They decided to try to run the ship aground on the beach.
passages.original: Ὅτε δὲ ἡμέρα ἐγένετο τὴν γῆν οὐκ ἐπεγίνωσκον κόλπον δέ τινα κατενόουν ἔχοντα αἰγιαλὸν εἰς ὃν ἐβουλεύοντο εἰ δύναιντο ἐξῶσαι τὸ πλοῖον

passages.text: Cutting away the anchors, they left them in the sea as they loosened the ropes that held the rudders. Then they hoisted the foresail to the wind and made for the beach.
passages.sermon:
The men were on a ship.
They cut away the anchors.
They left the anchors in the sea.
They loosened the ropes that held the rudders.
They hoisted the foresail to catch the wind.
They steered the ship toward the beach.
passages.original: καὶ τὰς ἀγκύρας περιελόντες εἴων εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν ἅμα ἀνέντες τὰς ζευκτηρίας τῶν πηδαλίων καὶ ἐπάραντες τὸν ἀρτέμωνα τῇ πνεούσῃ κατεῖχον εἰς τὸν αἰγιαλόν

passages.text: But the vessel struck a sandbar and ran aground. The bow stuck fast and would not move, and the stern was being broken up by the pounding of the waves.
passages.sermon:
A ship sailed into a place where two seas met.
The ship struck a sandbar.
The ship ran aground.
The front of the ship, called the bow, stuck fast.
The bow did not move.
The back of the ship, called the stern, broke apart.
Strong waves pounded the stern and broke it up.
passages.original: περιπεσόντες δὲ εἰς τόπον διθάλασσον ἐπέκειλαν τὴν ναῦν καὶ ἡ μὲν πρῷρα ἐρείσασα ἔμεινεν ἀσάλευτος ἡ δὲ πρύμνα ἐλύετο ὑπὸ τῆς βίας τῶν κυμάτων

passages.text: The soldiers planned to kill the prisoners so none of them could swim to freedom.
passages.sermon: The soldiers made a plan.\r\nThey wanted to kill the prisoners.\r\nThey did not want any prisoner to escape by swimming.
passages.original: Τῶν δὲ στρατιωτῶν βουλὴ ἐγένετο ἵνα τοὺς δεσμώτας ἀποκτείνωσιν μή τις ἐκκολυμβήσας διαφύγῃ

passages.text: But the centurion, wanting to spare Paul’s life, thwarted their plan. He commanded those who could swim to jump overboard first and get to land.
passages.sermon:
A centurion was in charge.
He wanted to save Paul’s life.
The soldiers planned to kill the prisoners.
The centurion stopped the soldiers from carrying out their plan.
He gave an order to the people who could swim.
He told the swimmers to jump overboard first.
He told them to go to land.
passages.original: ὁ δὲ ἑκατοντάρχης βουλόμενος διασῶσαι τὸν Παῦλον ἐκώλυσεν αὐτοὺς τοῦ βουλήματος ἐκέλευσέν τε τοὺς δυναμένους κολυμβᾶν ἀπορίψαντας πρώτους ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν ἐξιέναι

passages.text: The rest were to follow on planks and various parts of the ship. In this way everyone was brought safely to land.
passages.sermon:
Some people could not swim.
These people followed after the swimmers.
They used planks from the ship.
They also used other pieces from the ship.
Everyone reached the land safely.
